– the failing test (signature + snippet),

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test references a fixture class named SelfInstanceTwoVarsReflectionTestFixture, which likely exercises ToStringBuilder or related classes that involve ToStringStyle usage. The test calls validateNullToStringStyleRegistry(), implying it validates the state of some registry used by ToStringStyle.

The current bug report reveals a critical problem: ToStringStyle uses a ThreadLocal<WeakHashMap<Object,Object>> REGISTRY (code snippet line 137) to keep track of some state. This ThreadLocal object is created but never explicitly removed or cleaned up. Consequently, if a web application uses this library and then reloads (such as in some container environments), the lingering ThreadLocal reference can cause classloader memory leaks.

Inspection of the ToStringStyle.getRegistry() method shows that it returns the map stored in the current thread's ThreadLocal, or an empty map if none exists. However, no method exists to remove or clear this ThreadLocal state. The failing test likely triggers this lack of cleanup and exposes the stale thread-local data issue.

Recent bug reports do not mention this issue or related thread-local leaks, indicating that this is a relatively isolated problem in this module.

In summary, the bug is caused by improper lifecycle management of a thread-local REGISTRY in ToStringStyle. The thread-local variable is never removed, which leads to memory leaks in container environments where web apps are redeployed and classloaders held by thread-local references prevent garbage collection.

This diagnosis fully aligns with the current bug report's description and the failing test's focus on registry state validation. The underlying root cause is the absence of a method to clear or remove the ThreadLocal REGISTRY in ToStringStyle, causing memory leaks when the thread persists beyond the lifecycle of the context classloader.

This bug should be fixed by adding an API that clears the thread-local REGISTRY when it is no longer needed, and encouraging usage of that cleanup method in application or library lifecycle hooks. 

No evidence from recent unrelated bug reports contradicts this assessment.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
